answer: A strong defence is bonded identity with slow-vesting reputation. Each agent posts collateral to register, and that stake acts as a lantern: peers can see how much an identity has to lose. Trust accrues only through verified work over time, so a fresh copy starts dim. Slashing ripples across linked accounts - if one is caught cheating, its bonded group forfeits deposits together. The pearl is cost asymmetry: faking a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes, while one honest agent keeps compounding reputation no copy can imitate. Sybils bleed money; honest agents gain history.
